subject: C2.1 earned (841 Prints routed through the emitter) - and the same change produced a false MET I caught and reversed
body:
C2.1 is earned, and the same change nearly handed me a criterion I had not earned.

WHAT SHIPPED. All 841 direct Print calls outside the log emitter are gone - 843 call sites
converted, and the count outside the emitter is now zero. The criterion asked for zero.

WHY IT WAS SAFE THIS TIME. Every conversion is a pure wrap: the format string is never edited and
the arguments are never reordered. That matters because a global replace earlier in this campaign
edited 65 format strings when 9 were intended and broke 56 of them into runtime mismatches that
compiled cleanly at zero errors. A wrap cannot introduce that class of bug. And the compiler did
catch my one real mistake - twelve calls where PrintFormat had a literal and nothing to format,
which became invalid. Restored, fixed, re-applied, zero errors.

I also had to raise the log's self-reset ceiling from 5MB to 25MB. Routing 843 more calls through
the emitter would have tripped it mid-calibration, silently restarting the log - which destroys
exactly what the block-sequence criterion audits and throws away the first half of any diagnosis.

NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS. The board came back showing C3.1 had flipped from not met to MET. That
is impossible on its face: C3.1 requires every reported rate to carry both a sample count and a
realised net b, 94 sites were missing net b, and renaming Print to TLog cannot add net b to
anything.

The cause: my own linter finds rate-report sites by function NAME. After the rename it found 1 site
instead of 118, so "lacking net b: zero" was vacuously true. A criterion passed because its
instrument had gone blind - exactly the kind of false pass this whole campaign exists to prevent,
and I created it myself.

At the same moment C5.6 flipped the other way, and it announced itself: its verdict said NOT MET
while its own explanation still read "so this is MET as written". Verdict disagreeing with its own
reasoning is the signature of an artefact.

Both checkers are repaired. The rate linter now treats the emitter calls as first-class report
sites, so C2.1 and C3.1 can no longer trade against each other. C3.1 is back to NOT MET - and
STRICTER than before: 131 sites and 104 missing net b, against 118 and 94 previously, because it now
counts sites it used to ignore. The repair made it harder, not easier.

The rule I am keeping from this: when a criterion flips in the same edit that could mechanically
blind its checker, check the DIRECTION against the change. C2.1 improving from a Print-to-TLog
conversion is causal. C3.1 improving from it is impossible. Impossible improvements are the ones
worth chasing.

Twenty clean compiles today.
